lead: Rules 19 to 23 fill the gaps in the right-of-way rules: passing an obstruction together, tacking off a shore with a boat on your hip, and boats that are returning, doing turns, capsized or not racing.

qa.q: Is an anchored boat or a rock an obstruction under the racing rules?
qa.a: Yes: an **obstruction** is any object you could not pass without a substantial change of course if you sailed straight at it from one hull length away, such as an anchored vessel, a pier or a rock.

blocks.p: An **obstruction** is an object you could not pass without a substantial change of course if you sailed straight at it from one hull length away: an anchored vessel, a pier, a rock, buoyed or not. So is an area the sailing instructions close to boats. A boat racing is one only to boats that must keep clear of her or, under rule 22, avoid her.

fig.note: B on starboard is an obstruction to both port-tack boats

blocks.p: Rule 19 does not apply at a mark you both must leave on the same side: there rule 18 governs, or neither rule at a starting mark as you approach to start. Nor is a third boat an obstruction between two boats to whom rule 18 applies when she overlaps each of them.

qa.q: Rule 19: who gives room at an obstruction when two boats are overlapped?
qa.a: The outside boat: under **rule 19** she gives the inside boat room between her and the obstruction, right of way or not, unless she has been unable to since the overlap began. The right-of-way boat chooses the side.

blocks.p: The **right-of-way boat chooses** the side on which to pass; if she changes course to do it, she gives the other boat room to keep clear. When the boats are **overlapped**, the outside boat gives the inside boat room between her and the obstruction, right of way or not, unless she has been unable to since the overlap began. Room is seamanlike space for the conditions, current included, and no wider.

tiles.name: Along a sea wall
tiles.note: A squeezes in with no room: no rights

blocks.p: A **continuing obstruction** is one you sail alongside for a while: a shore, a sea wall, a line of moored boats. There a boat clear astern may take an inside overlap only if there is room to pass between the other boat and the obstruction when the overlap begins. If not, she gets no room and must keep clear while the overlap lasts; rules 10 and 11 do not help her. Rule 19, not 18, applies there even if it is a mark.

sections.title: Room to tack at an obstruction

qa.q: When can I hail "Room to tack" near the shore, and what must the other boat do?
qa.a: Under **rule 20**, when close-hauled or above and soon needing a substantial course change to avoid an obstruction safely. The hailed boat on the same tack tacks as soon as possible, or replies "You tack" and gives you room.

blocks.p: Close-hauled towards a shore with a boat close to windward, you cannot tack without fouling her. Rule 20 lets you hail **"Room to tack"** to a boat on the same tack, overlapped or not, but only when you are approaching an obstruction, will soon need a substantial course change to avoid it safely, and are sailing close-hauled or above.

fig.note: You hail; A tacks or answers "You tack"

list: You hail, then give her time to respond.
She must respond even to a hail she thinks wrong: her remedy is a protest.
She tacks as soon as possible, or at once replies "You tack" and gives you room to tack and avoid her.
Once she responds, you tack as soon as possible.

blocks.p: A hailed boat blocked by a third boat hails her in turn. Where a hail may not be heard, add a clear signal; the notice of race may prescribe one. Do not hail at a mark if a boat fetching it would have to change course. A hail does nothing to a boat on the other tack. From your hail until you have tacked clear, rule 18.2 is off between you.

sections.title: Boats that give up their rights

qa.q: Rule 21: who keeps clear when a boat returns to start after the gun?
qa.a: The returning boat: from her starting signal until her hull is completely on the pre-start side she **keeps clear** of boats not doing the same, and rules 10 to 13 are off between them. So does a boat taking a penalty.

blocks.p: Three kinds of boat keep clear of any boat not doing the same, and Section A (rules 10 to 13) is off between them.

fig.note: Returning after the start: keep clear of A and B

blocks.p: Over the line before the gun you still have your ordinary rights: rule 21.1 begins at your starting signal. A boat that was over and sails on is not returning and keeps her rights.

sections.title: Boats you must avoid

qa.q: Rule 22: do I have to keep clear of a capsized or anchored boat?
qa.a: Yes, if possible: under **rule 22** you avoid a boat that is capsized, anchored, aground or helping someone in danger, whatever her tack. She counts as capsized when her masthead is in the water.

refs: RRS 22, RRS 45, RRS Part 2 Section D preamble
RRS 22, RRS Part 2 Section D preamble

blocks.p: If possible, avoid a boat that is **capsized** or has not regained control after capsizing, is **anchored** or **aground**, or is **trying to help** a person or vessel in danger. Her tack is irrelevant: Section A is off. A boat is capsized when her masthead is in the water; knocked flat with the mast clear she is an ordinary boat, and once she sails under control again the normal rules return.

fig.note: A is capsized dead ahead: avoid her if possible

blocks.p: Anchoring while racing is allowed, and a boat you must avoid is an obstruction. "If possible" is meant: capsized yourself, you break nothing. A two-turns penalty clears a breach; a boat that stopped to help may ask for redress.

sections.title: Keeping out of other boats' races

qa.q: After I finish, can I sail through boats that are still racing?
qa.a: Not if you would interfere: under **rule 23.1**, a boat that is not racing must not interfere with a boat that is racing, if reasonably possible. Finished, retired or waiting for your start, go round the fleet.

blocks.p: You are **racing** from your preparatory signal until you have finished and cleared the finishing line and marks, or retired. At other times rule 23.1 applies: if reasonably possible, do not interfere with a boat that is racing. Finished, retired or waiting for your start, go round the fleet.

fig.note: You have finished and cleared the line: stay out of A's way

blocks.p: Rule 23.2 protects a boat taking a penalty, a boat on another leg and a boat returning to start: do not interfere with them if reasonably possible. After your starting signal it does not bind you while you sail your proper course, but rule 10 still does. A boat that will be scored OCS is still racing, with full rights.
